shots.subject: Live football play mid-field, dark jerseys vs white jerseys, ball carrier and pursuing defenders
shots.note: Clearest visibility of the whole reel — real game action in daylight; distant wide angle, no faces, good only as context B-roll.

shots.subject: Dead-ball lull — players clustered near sideline, a lone defensive back standing in space
shots.note: No athletic action; a huddle/reset moment. Off-brief for a hype cut.

shots.subject: Ball carrier breaking upfield into open space with defenders in pursuit
shots.note: Best-lit athletic moment — a runner in space. Strongest daylight highlight, though SD and distant.

shots.subject: End-zone / corner action shot through a foreground chain-link fence, players leaping
shots.note: Chain-link fence bisects the frame in the foreground — unusable no matter how good the play behind it is.

shots.subject: Dusk game action — tackle in progress, runners and spread defenders across the field
shots.note: Golden-dusk light adds warmth; real tackles and runs, but still distant and softening as light drops.

shots.subject: Line-of-scrimmage formations and snaps, both squads set at the trenches
shots.note: Formation/snap moments — useful to show the trench and team size; static and low-energy on their own, good as connective tissue.

shots.subject: Night floodlit plays — short-yardage snaps and an open-field carry with pursuit
shots.lighting: artificial floodlights, dark surround, some motion blur
shots.note: Night-game 'Friday lights' feel is on-brief; open-field run near the end is the pick here. Dark + motion-blurred by the SD source.

shots.subject: Night piles and scrums near the sideline, players stacking up, spectators behind
shots.note: Mostly pile-ups and aftermath — messy and dark, reads as clutter rather than highlight.

shots.subject: Night line-of-scrimmage set, then a ball carrier breaking free downfield with blockers ahead
shots.note: Ends on a downfield breakaway with lead blockers — the best night-game highlight beat, though dark and low-res.

summary: Single elevated sideline camera (Hudl-style game film) of one full American-football game, 480x360 SD, running from overcast daylight into floodlit night. Content is squarely on-brief — real game action, tackles, snaps, and a couple of breakaway runs — but the footage is distant, faceless, low-resolution, and increasingly dark and motion-blurred in the night second half. Usable as action/context B-roll to establish 'real games, real team,' not as hero close-ups; no crowd, sideline, or portrait energy that a recruiting trailer leans on hardest. Best beats are the daylight breakaway (~35s) and the night downfield breakaway near the end.
